trigger: A hospital report, researcher report, or other information alleging a device failed to meet its specifications (including a security failure)
deadline: Record on receipt; review, evaluate, and investigate (no fixed day count in the regulation; internal target: complaint opened within 1 business day)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - every product security event is screened as a possible complaint

trigger: Information that reasonably suggests a device may have caused or contributed to a death or serious injury, or malfunctioned in a way likely to do so if it recurred (a compromised device that alters alarms or infusion settings can be such a malfunction)
deadline: No later than 30 calendar days after the company becomes aware

trigger: An MDR reportable event needs remedial action to prevent an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to public health, or FDA asks in writing
deadline: No later than 5 work days after becoming aware
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if remedial action is needed
clock_starts: Becoming aware of the need for remedial action

trigger: New information not known when the initial MDR was filed
deadline: Within 30 calendar days of receiving the information
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if an MDR was filed

trigger: Company initiates a correction or removal (for example, a firmware fix, key rotation, or field action) to reduce a risk to health posed by the device or to remedy a violation that may present a risk to health
deadline: Within 10 working days of initiating the correction or removal (not required if already reported under Part 803 or exempt under 806.1(b))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - unless all FDA enforcement-discretion conditions below are met
clock_starts: Initiation of the correction or removal

obligation: Record of a correction or removal not reported
trigger: Correction or removal that is not reportable (routine cybersecurity update for a controlled risk, or the enforcement-discretion path)
deadline: Keep the record with the justification, reviewed by a designated person; retain 2 years beyond the expected life of the device

obligation: Uncontrolled cybersecurity risk: customer communication (FDA enforcement-discretion condition)
citation: FDA postmarket cybersecurity guidance (December 2016), section VII.B (nonbinding)
trigger: Vulnerability assessed as an uncontrolled risk to safety and essential performance, with no known serious adverse events or deaths
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after learning of the vulnerability: tell customers and users, give compensating controls, and describe the remediation plan
notify: Hospital customers and user community; the ISAO (copy)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - guidance, not a regulation; meeting all conditions means FDA does not intend to enforce 806 reporting

obligation: Uncontrolled cybersecurity risk: fix distributed (FDA enforcement-discretion condition)
citation: FDA postmarket cybersecurity guidance (December 2016), section VII.B (nonbinding)
trigger: Same as above
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 60 days after learning of the vulnerability: fix, validate, and distribute a deployable fix

obligation: ISAO participation and sharing (FDA enforcement-discretion condition)
citation: FDA postmarket cybersecurity guidance (December 2016), sections VII.B and IX (nonbinding)
trigger: Company communicates with customers about a vulnerability
deadline: Share the customer communication with the ISAO when customers are notified
notify: ISAO that shares medical device vulnerabilities

trigger: Critical vulnerability that could cause uncontrolled risks in a cyber device or related system
deadline: Make updates and patches available out of cycle as soon as possible (no day count in the statute)
notify: Hospital customers (update service or field service)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for devices submitted after 524B took effect (VM-700, DG-10, CR-100, HB-40, IV-300 v2); legacy devices follow the postmarket guidance

trigger: A researcher, ISAO, or customer reports a vulnerability
deadline: Acknowledge within 3 business days; agree a public disclosure date
notify: Reporter; optionally CISA for a coordinated advisory

obligation: Business associate breach notice to customers
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI held in the DDC, RCM platform, or a DG-10 gateway cache the company maintains for customers
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery; include each affected individual's identity to the extent possible and other information the customer needs; shorter BAA terms apply
notify: Each affected hospital or practice (covered entity) through the BAA contact
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any employee, officer, or agent (164.410(a)(2))

obligation: Security incident report under the BAA
trigger: Any security incident involving customer PHI of which the company becomes aware
deadline: As set in each BAA (5 to 30 days in current BAAs); check the BAA terms register (POAM-022)

trigger: A law enforcement official states that notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: Delay for the period stated in writing; up to 30 days if the statement is oral and documented
notify: Hold customer notices; document the request

trigger: Customer determines a breach occurred
deadline: Customer's deadlines; the company supplies information promptly
notify: Individuals, HHS, media, state regulators (by the customer)
applies_at_this_tier: No - customer duty; the company supports

trigger: A subcontractor that handles PHI for the company discovers a breach
deadline: Per the subcontractor BAA (10 days in the company template) and no later than 60 days after the subcontractor's discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 62 subcontractors (5 without current BAAs until POAM-022 closes)

trigger: Breach of security of unsecured PHR identifiable health information in the consumer app (unauthorized acquisition, including an unauthorized disclosure)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected U.S. individual by written notice (email if the individual chose email as the primary method; substitute notice if contact information is insufficient for 10 or more)
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known or reasonably should have been known to any employee, officer, or agent (318.3(c))

obligation: FTC rule notice to the FTC (500 or more)
trigger: Breach of security involving 500 or more individuals
deadline: Contemporaneously with the notice to individuals

trigger: Breaches of security involving fewer than 500 individuals
deadline: Log sent annually no later than 60 calendar days after the end of the calendar year
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - consumer app (log not yet kept; POAM-021)

trigger: PHR identifiable health information of 500 or more residents of a state or jurisdiction is, or is reasonably believed to have been, acquired
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets serving that state or jurisdiction
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the threshold is met

obligation: FTC rule third party service provider notice (inbound)
trigger: A service provider to the consumer app discovers a breach
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after the provider's discovery; the provider must obtain acknowledgment
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the company must first tell its providers it is a vendor of personal health records (POAM-021)

trigger: A law enforcement official determines that notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: Delay as provided under 45 CFR 164.528(a)(2)

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information the company owns (workforce records, consumer app users)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
applies_at_this_tier: Always check. Apply the law of each state where affected residents live

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: State-specific thresholds
deadline: Varies by state

obligation: State agent notice to the data owner
citation: State breach notification statutes (agent or service provider provisions)
trigger: Breach of a system the company maintains for a customer that owns the personal information
deadline: Varies by state; plan to the shortest (Florida worked example below: 10 days)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - DDC and RCM hold customers' patients' information

trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains as a third-party agent for a Florida hospital or practice
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after determining the breach or having reason to believe it occurred; give the customer the information it needs
notify: Each affected customer (the covered entity under 501.171)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - shorter than the HIPAA 60-day limit, so it sets the clock for Florida customers
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred

trigger: Breach of security of personal information (includes medical information) of Florida residents that the company owns (workforce, consumer app users)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (law enforcement delay under 501.171(4)(b))
notify: Affected Florida residents by mail or email
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay

trigger: Cybersecurity incident discovered that could be material, including a PSIRT severity-1 fielded-device incident
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery (the disclosure committee convenes within 48 hours under POL-03 4.7)
notify: Disclosure committee (General Counsel chairs); record the date and time of the determination

trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing): material aspects of the nature, scope, and timing, and the material impact or reasonably likely material impact

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Up to 30 days after the original due date; up to 30 more days on a further determination; in extraordinary circumstances a final period of up to 60 days (national security only)
notify: Department of Justice (through outside counsel); SEC notified by the Attorney General
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the Attorney General so determines

trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the next Form 10-K; update the description of processes and of any material effects of incidents

trigger: Disclosure committee convenes on a possibly material incident
deadline: Same day the committee convenes
notify: Committee members, responders with knowledge, and executives (special blackout notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company policy, not a regulatory deadline

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); FBI or CISA

trigger: Criminal exploitation of devices or systems, or extortion
deadline: As early as practical
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; the proposed criteria would cover manufacturers of class II or III devices, so recheck when final

trigger: Suspected security incident with possible loss
deadline: Per policy (use the carrier hotline before hiring vendors)

trigger: Service outage or security incident affecting customer services
deadline: Per contract (service status updates every 2 hours during an outage; security incident notice per BAA)
owner: Vice President, Digital Health; Vice President, Remote Monitoring Services

obligation: DoD cyber incident reporting for covered defense information
trigger: Cyber incident affecting covered defense information
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no defense contracts

citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts
